option.title: אמא ואבא, 5 דברים שיעזרו לי לא לוותר
option.angle: אלון, בן 5, רוצה לזרוק הכל כשהמגדל נופל שוב. הוא מבקש מההורים חמישה דברים: להגיד שהם רואים שקשה, לחלק לחלק קטן, הפסקה של חיבוק וספר ואז לחזור, לשאול מה עוד אפשר לנסות בלי לבנות במקומו, ומילה על המאמץ ולא רק על התוצאה. בסוף: לדבר אחרי שנרגע על מה ננסה מחר.
option.target_parent: הורים לילד בן 4 עד 7 שזורק משימה ברגע הראשון שקשה לו.

hook.gap: Which five things help a 5-year-old boy keep trying when his tower falls again and he wants to quit?

slides.headline:
אמא ואבא
5 דברים שיעזרו לי
לא לוותר
slides.body: כשקשה לי, ואני רוצה לזרוק הכל

slides.headline: המגדל נפל, שוב
slides.body:
בניתי אותו גבוה, כמעט עד השולחן.
ואז קובייה אחת זזה, והכל נפל.
אני בועט בקוביות וצועק ״אני לא יכול!״
אבל בפנים אני **רוצה** להצליח.

scene.action: The boy kicks at a pile of fallen wooden blocks on the rug with an angry, teary face, while his parents look up from the sofa.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a woven rug, a low wooden shelf, a beige sofa, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 1: לראות שקשה לי
slides.headline: קודם, תגידו שאתם רואים
slides.body:
כשאומרים לי ״זה קל, נו״,
אני רק כועס יותר.
כשאתם אומרים ״אני רואה שזה קשה לך״,
משהו בי נרגע, ואני מוכן **לשמוע**.

scene.action: His mother sits down on the rug next to the boy and puts a gentle hand on his back, looking at the fallen blocks with him.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a woven rug, a low wooden shelf, a beige sofa, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 2: חלק קטן
slides.headline: רק את השורה הראשונה
slides.body:
לא כל המגדל.
רק שלוש קוביות.
ואז עוד שלוש.
פתאום זה **אפשרי**.

scene.action: The boy carefully stacks just three wooden blocks on the rug, his tongue out in concentration, his father kneeling beside him.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a woven rug, a low wooden shelf, a beige sofa, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 3: הפסקה של חיבוק
slides.headline: מה עושים כשאני מתפוצץ?
slides.body:
אני כבר זורק, צועק, בוכה.
## מה יעזור לי:
הפסקה קטנה. חיבוק על הספה, ספר אחד,
ואחר כך חוזרים לקוביות **עם כוח חדש**.

scene.action: The boy snuggles between his parents on the sofa looking at a picture book together, the blocks waiting on the rug.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a woven rug, a low wooden shelf, a beige sofa, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 4: לאמן, לא לבנות
slides.headline: אל תבנו במקומי
slides.body:
כשאתם בונים לי, זה כבר לא שלי.
## מה יעזור לי לשמוע:
> ״מה עוד אפשר לנסות, אלון?״
ואולי להראות לי דרך **אחת**,
ולתת לי להמשיך לבד.

scene.action: His father points at a wide flat block as the base while the boy places it himself, his father's hands resting on his knees.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a woven rug, a low wooden shelf, a beige sofa, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 5: מילה על הניסיון
slides.headline: ״ניסית שוב ושוב״
slides.body:
## מה אתם רואים:
מגדל עקום, שעוד לא גמור.
## מה קורה לי בפנים:
אני מחכה לשמוע שראיתם **שניסיתי**.
לא רק ״איזה יפה יצא״.

scene.action: The boy stands proudly next to a crooked half-built block tower while both parents give him a warm thumbs up.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a woven rug, a low wooden shelf, a beige sofa, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.headline: אני לא מוותר, קשה לי
slides.body:
ואחרי שנרגעתי, תשאלו אותי
מה היה הכי קשה, ומה ננסה מחר.
ככה אני חוזר לקוביות,
ולא **בורח** מהן.

scene.action: In pyjamas, the boy talks with his mother on his bed in the evening, both looking at the block tower on the floor.
scene.setting: The boy's small Israeli bedroom in the evening: a low bed, a block tower on the floor, a plain warm cream wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.headline:
אפשר גם לעזור להם
עם הרצון לוותר
בעזרת ספר מותאם אישית.
slides.body:
תכתבו "ויתור"
ואשלח לכם קישור להכנת הספר

sources.title: Parenting Strategies for a Child Who is Easily Frustrated
sources.quote: When your child falls apart, let her know that you appreciate how hard it can be. ... Then become her coach—help your child think through solutions without doing the work for her. ... Suggest or demonstrate strategies for solving whatever problem she is facing. ... Break the challenge into manageable parts. ... Offer time away from the frustrating task for a hug or a cozy snuggle with a book. ... Then return to the challenge with new energy.
sources.supports: Acknowledge how hard it is, coach instead of doing it for the child, suggest or show a strategy, break the challenge into parts, offer a break with a hug and return with new energy.

sources.title: How to Help Kids Learn to Fail
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute (last reviewed or updated 6 May 2025)
sources.quote: When your kid does fail at something, let them know you see how frustrated and disappointed they are. ... Skipping right to bouncing back doesn't give kids the time they need to feel their feelings. ... When your kid is ready, talk about what went wrong and how they might do things differently next time. ... You and your child can try to come up with what they could do the next time for a better chance at success.
sources.supports: Name the frustration first, give time to feel it, and when the child is ready talk about what to do differently next time.

sources.title: How to Support Young Kids Who Are Struggling in School
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute (last reviewed or updated 7 Nov 2025, Rae Jacobson)
sources.quote: Help kids build their resilience by doing small bursts of difficult work ... Praising your child’s efforts instead of focusing on results will help them feel more comfortable trying things ... Managing frustration without blowing up, or giving up, is an essential skill for kids (and grownups)
sources.supports: Short bursts of difficult work build resilience, and praising effort rather than results makes trying feel safer. The page is about school; applied here to any hard task at home.

sources.title: Recommended Reading: Books to Teach Kids About Feelings & Resilience
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org, American Academy of Pediatrics (last updated 24 Apr 2025)
sources.quote: Reading books together about common feelings can help children recognize their own emotions. It can also help them develop empathy, understanding how others may be feeling.
sources.supports: Reading together about feelings helps children recognise their own and understand others'. Used only as support for reading stories about a hard moment; no promise of a result.
